despatch_jan1740.summary: Höpken and Carlson report to the King how the Porte's dragoman brought the signed defensive alliance treaty and asked to delay its exchange and keep it secret, how they argued for a prompt exchange, and how the exemplars were exchanged on 14/25 January 1740 after a present to Ragib Efendi. They credit the King's firmness over the Russian frontier, note the French ambassador's late help, and ask for a provisional instruction and full powers.
despatch_jan1740.en:
[image 321]
(Marked "Duplicate"; archive date 15/26 Jan. 1740; chancery note, first word doubtful: read in the Council 10 April
1740.) Most Mighty, Most Gracious King! In our last despatch, which was of the 5/16 of this month to Your Royal Majesty
and the Council of the Realm and to the President, the high-born Count Carl Gyllenborg, of which we humbly enclose the
duplicate, Your Royal Majesty will graciously have had laid before him how the exchange of the defensive alliance was
put off from day to day. (No. 2.)

[image 322]
and what we supposed [to be] the cause, and more.

lita_1741.summary: The more one examines the last peace treaty between the Porte and the Muscovites, the more one finds conditions onerous and unbearable for the Sultan, manifest contradictions, and attempts to deceive the Porte, which the Muscovites treated as an inferior prince on whom they meant to impose laws; this is to be shown article by article, beginning with article 2 on the frontiers (breaks off).
lita_1741.en:
English of readinglita1741.md (notes as there).

The more one looks at and examines the last treaty of peace made between the Porte and the Muscovites, the more one
finds in it not only conditions onerous and unbearable for the Sultan, but also (the cipher has "couvre" for
"découvre") manifest contradictions, and that every means was sought to deceive the Ottoman Porte, with which the
Muscovites dealt, with the Sultan, not as with an equal prince but as with an inferior prince, and on whom they meant
to impose laws.

This will be proved by examining the articles of the said treaty, as follows, namely:

In the 2nd article it is said that the frontiers shall be the same as they were before, and as they were settled by
the earlier treaties. These words are clear, but in order to be able ...

castellane_oct1741.summary: After a general divan at the Porte, the Porte's dragoman invited Castellane on behalf of the Grand Vizier to a kind of congress next Sunday at which Monsieur de Romanzof (probably Rumyantsev, the Russian ambassador) is to be present; he asks the Swedes for their reflections before the sieur de Laria goes to the Porte's dragoman next morning at eight.
castellane_oct1741.en:
English of readingcastellaneoct1741.md, with the same marks. [?...] = the French word rests partly on a guessed value.

Letter of the comte de Castellane.

There [?was] [?today] a general divan at the Porte; after this divan the dragoman of the Porte came to invite me, on
behalf of the Grand Vizier, to go [?next] Sunday to a kind of con{ha/grè}ss, at which [?Monsieur] de [?Romanzof] is
to be present.

If you have, [?Monsieur], any [?reflections] to [?communicate] to me concerning your interests, I would be
[?delighted] to be able to receive them before the [?sieur] de Laria [?goes] to the dragoman of the Porte, [?where]
he is to go tomorrow at eight o'clock in the morning.

[?I have] etc. (the formula is cut short in the copy)

Notes. "Romanzof" is very probably Aleksandr Ivanovich Rumyantsev, Russian ambassador at the Porte in 1740-41;

reply_oct1741.summary: The Swedes thank Castellane for his generous conduct toward the interests of their court, announce a visit next evening to set out their thoughts on Sweden's present interests with regard to Russia and Russia's differences with the Porte, and begin to say that in Sweden's critical situation with Russia any accommodation between the Porte and Russia is ... (breaks off at the foot of the page).
reply_oct1741.en:
English of readingreplyoct1741.md, with the same marks. [?...] = the French word rests partly on a guessed value;
[1515] = a group left unread.

Our reply to the comte de Castellane.

We receive at this moment the letter that Your Excellency did us the honour of writing to us yesterday evening, and
we have been most deeply touched with [?joy] and gratitude at the [?generous] conduct of [?Your] Excellency
concerning the interests of our Court, to which no one in this country [1515] is better able to contribute than an
ambassador of France.

We [?intend] to go tomorrow evening, [?God] willing, to [?Your] Excellency, to have the honour of setting out to you
at length our thoughts on the present interests of Sweden with regard to Russia and [?on the] differences of the
latter with the Porte.
